newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa faces tough times ahead - World Bank.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa faces tough times ahead - World Bank.

text.p: South Africa faces tough times ahead as it seeks to guarantee a stable and prosperous future for a population still sufering from the legacy of its racist apartheid past, the World Bank said on Monday.

"While much has been done on the political front to dismantle inequalities, the country faces formidable challenges in redressing the entrenched impacts of apartheid," World Bank South African representitive Judith Edstrom said.
Edstrom was writing in the latest edition of International Policy Update, a magazine published by the South African Institute of International Affairs.
The World Bank has acted in an advisory capacity to the African National Congress-led government of President Nelson Mandela, which swept to power in the country's first all-race elections in 1994.
Edstrom said that the country faced four main problem areas:
* Economic growth must accelerate from the current three percent level to six percent and at the same time become more labour absorbing.
* Poverty needs to be reduced and delivery of essential services, such as education and health, needs to be improved and previously disadvantaged groups need better access to housing and land.
* The shortage of skills in areas such as public sector management and economic development policy needs to be increased.
* South Africa must clearly determine what its regional role will be in developing its neighbours' economies.
"Opportunities must be created for previously disadvantaged groups, above all employment and education...living standards must be raised and services provided," Edstrom said.
South Africa is currently talking with the World Bank about funding for a Department of Trade and Industry development programme, but Edstrom gave no indications of the current status of the talks.
